title: Bug: Check intermittently red on dev - a git child in a code-map run is killed (signal SIGTERM) and reported as an error
description:
NOT STARTED. Check fails intermittently on dev itself and on PRs, on the Linux runner; Docs, Package and Tracker integrity stay green. Signature: GlyphError 'git -c did not report an exit status (signal SIGTERM)' thrown from guarded() at src/codemap.ts:441 via buildCodeMap (codemap.ts:552) and produceCodeMap (codemap.ts:397), called from test/parity.test.ts:162. A second signature, test/stream.test.ts (a cold CLI subprocess took 5.1 s and bun's 5 s default killed it, code-map exit code null), is addressed by glyph-cli#102 (bunfig.toml test timeout 60 s plus setDefaultTimeout in test/stream.test.ts), which does NOT fix the parity signature.
Evidence (run ids and Check job ids): run 45100876753 job 137451193804 (dev after #99, codemap.ts:441); run 45101234884 job 137452308091 (dev after #100, test/stream.test.ts:266); run 45101379493 jobs 137452769988 and 137453705490 (#101, stream test, code-map exit null); run 45101738310 job 137453907838 (#102 head 5f488ba, parity, SIGTERM); run 45102143367 job 137455186669 (#102 head a302282 with the 60 s timeout, parity again). Loaded-runner timing: Check took 2m20 to 3m on the failing runs against about 1m05 on earlier green ones, and several PR runs overlapped.
HYPOTHESIS, NOT SHOWN: spawnLimits (src/git.ts) caps a git read's timeout at the remaining wall-time budget with Math.max(1, ceil(left)). When the child is killed at that cap, proc.timedOut is false and proc.signal is SIGTERM; stopIfBudgetSpent(budgeted) then throws BudgetExpired only if activeBudget.expired() has already flipped. A kill at the deadline's rounding edge leaves expired() false and the read becomes an indeterminate error instead of a stop. What is NOT shown: that the budget is the cause (the parity run might use no budget at all), that the pre-GCLI-46 Bun.spawnSync path behaved differently, or that load alone explains it. Reproduce before fixing.

acceptanceCriteria.text: the failure is reproduced locally, for example by running test/parity.test.ts repeatedly under CPU load, and the reproduction (command, load, failure rate, the error text) is recorded in the task notes (proof: the recorded command and its failing output)

the root cause is identified from the reproduction and recorded, stating whether the code-map time budget, a git timeout, or something else sent the SIGTERM (proof: a note naming the cause with the evidence that distinguishes it from the other two)

only after the cause is recorded: a fix in src/codemap.ts and src/git.ts, with a test that forces a tiny budget and proves a stop (truncated, not an error) (proof: the test fails without the fix and passes with it)
a mutation proof that the new test goes red when the fix is removed (proof: recorded mutation run naming the failing test)
the fix landed with an Opus review at the exact head (proof: review verdict recorded in the task notes)

implementationNotes: FINDING B IS A SILENT WRONG RESULT, NOT AN ERROR (leader instruction 2026-11-23): git grep exits 0 with empty stdout and stderr, grepLines turns that into lineRanges [] with rangesRead true, so there is no budget row and no omission. The same blind spot applies to every git read in src/codemap.ts. The diagnostic PR (fix/GCLI-51-no-exit-status-diagnostic) only adds elapsed ms, timeout cap and budget left to the 'did not report an exit status' message; it does NOT fix finding B and does not change that behaviour. OPEN ITEM FOR opum-doc (changes the product contract, not decided here): decide whether a git read that exits 0 with empty output where output is expected should be treated as suspicious (an indeterminate error) or retried.

2026-11-23 reproduction attempt (worker, local macOS, bun 1.3.14, 10 cores; script: N busy 'while :; do :; done' loops, then bun test test/parity.test.ts repeated). NOT YET REPRODUCED: the SIGTERM signature ('git -c did not report an exit status (signal SIGTERM)') did not occur in any run. Measured: (a) default 5 s bun test timeout, 30 loops: 5/5 runs fail, each at 'hostile global config gives the same bytes' with 'this test timed out after 5000ms' (7.9-9.0 s) - the #102 signature, not SIGTERM. (b) bun test --timeout 60000: 30 loops 5/5 green; 150 loops, bun 1.3.14, 10 runs: 2 red, both a DIFFERENT fault: byte mismatch against the golden with EMPTY omissions (a pointer's lineRanges [] where the golden has ['line 1'], once on file-cap, once on special-paths; confirmed by a temporary console.error of output.omissions, reverted) - so under load the code map can return a wrong, non-truncated output with no time-budget row; unexplained, needs its own root cause. 150 loops, bun 1.4.4 (homebrew; CI pins 1.4.2): 6/6 green. EVIDENCE AGAINST THE HYPOTHESIS: spawnSync's own timeout sets error.code ETIMEDOUT on bun 1.3.14, bun 1.4.4 and node, so a kill at the budget cap reaches git() in src/codemap.ts with proc.timedOut TRUE and the message would read '(timeout)'. The failing CI text reads '(signal SIGTERM)', i.e. timedOut false: the SIGTERM did not come from spawnSync's timeout. The only other documented source in src/spawn.ts is a maxBuffer overflow (ENOBUFS; GIT_MAX_BUFFER is 32 MiB in codemap.ts, implausible for the fixtures) - otherwise an external SIGTERM to the child. So the budget-rounding hypothesis is contradicted by the error text itself; the sender is still unidentified. Next: find what could SIGTERM a git child on the CI runner, reproduce with the CI-pinned bun 1.4.2 (not installed locally; an unpinned npx download was refused by the permission layer and was not retried).

FINDING B (separate from the SIGTERM signature; measured 2026-11-23, local, bun 1.3.14, 150 busy loops, test/parity.test.ts with --timeout 60000, temporary console.error instrumentation in grepLines reverted): the wrong-output fault is a git grep that exits 0 with EMPTY stdout and EMPTY stderr. In grepLines (src/codemap.ts:306) status 0 with no stdout parses to no ranges, so the pointer is returned with lineRanges [] and rangesRead true: no time-budget row, no omission, reason unchanged, i.e. a silently wrong result. Seen as 'REPRO-GREP0-EMPTY' + 'REPRO-GREP0-NOLINES' (status 0, stdout '', stderr ''): 7 failing runs of 40 across the instrumented batches, on identifiers alphaWidget, ledgerTotals, longPathMarkerA/B. Re-running the IDENTICAL git grep immediately afterwards (same spawn path) returned status 0 with the full stdout (478 and 90 bytes) in all 4 retried cases, so the fault is transient. Not reproduced in isolation: 3 x 3000 spawnSync('echo hello') under the same load on bun 1.3.14, bun 1.4.4 and node, 0 empty stdout, 0 non-zero. So it is NOT yet attributed: it is either bun's spawnSync dropping stdout of a successful child, or git itself, and only git-specific probing can say; the retry shows the output exists and is deterministic when read again. Consequence: any git read in src/codemap.ts can silently return empty on a loaded host, so a successful empty read cannot be told from a lost one; GCLI-51's fix scope must cover this fault in addition to (or instead of) the SIGTERM one.

CORRECTION to FINDING B counts: across the four 10-run batches (40 runs) the empty-stdout event was logged 9 times (1, 4, 0 and 4 per batch; one earlier uninstrumented batch is not counted), and 8 of 40 runs ended red; not every red run carried a logged event, and some reds in the hostile-config test were not attributed. The '7 of 40' above is wrong. Only 4 events had the immediate retry logged; all 4 retried clean.

2026-11-23 glyph-cli#107 landed as 8849dfa (Opus APPROVE at head aad067b, claude-opus-5-5; the reviewer read files only). #107 does NOT fix the intermittent SIGTERM; it only adds timing to the error message, so GCLI-51 stays open with a diagnostic, not a fix. Reviewer observations: (1) the parity test runs under the default 7 s budget (test/parity.test.ts lines 154 and 162 call produceCodeMap without timeBudgetMs; CODE_MAP_TIME_BUDGET_MS is 7_000), so the next failure's 'timeout cap' should read below 7000. (2) The CI text says 'signal SIGTERM', so timedOut was false: either bun's node:child_process.spawnSync does not report ETIMEDOUT on a timeout kill the way node does (scripts/node-spawn-check.mjs measured node only; my local probe on bun 1.3.14 and 1.4.4 did report ETIMEDOUT, CI pins 1.4.2), or the SIGTERM came from outside the process. The next failure's elapsed time decides it: close to the cap points to bun, well under the cap points to an external signal. (3) Nit: the existing B2 test in test/codemap-budget.test.ts already executes the real kill path and asserts only the error type, not the new text.

2026-11-23 NODE MEASUREMENT for DEC-299 (a5) (worker, local macOS, 10 cores). OBJECT MEASURED: the packed Node bundle dist/glyph.js built by 'npm run build' from commit 8ff960b (fix(GCLI-56)), run by node v24.22.2 (not bun). LOAD: 150 busy 'while :; do :; done' sh loops (15x cores). HARNESS: a git wrapper first on PATH logs every git invocation (class, exit, stdout bytes) of the node-run glyph, and each run's stdout and exit code are compared with a baseline taken before the run set (two baseline runs equal). Per run: 'glyph code-map --source-ref main --json' (stdin task text naming a path, 3 identifiers and a plain token; exercises rev-parse, cat-file, merge-base, diff, grep -l, grep -n and the index build) and 'glyph callers helper07 --json' (exercises ls-files and cat-file --batch in src/git.ts), each with a fresh GLYPH_CACHE_DIR. RESULT, 60 runs x 2 commands = 120 command runs, 1500 git reads (rev-parse 300, cat-file 120, merge-base 60, diff names 120, diff ranges 240, grep -l 180, grep -n 240, ls-files 60, cat-file --batch 60, other 120): 0 reads with exit 0 and empty stdout at the git level (baseline also has 0 legitimate empties in this repo), 0 outputs differing from the baseline, 0 exit 7, 0 other exits. DETECTABLE RATE: 0 of 1500 reads and 0 of 120 command runs; by the rule of three the 95% upper bound is about 2e-3 per read and 2.5% per command run, so the sample could NOT have shown a fault rarer than about 1 in 500 reads; the bun-run fault measured earlier (9 events in 40 parity runs on bun 1.3.14) could not be called absent on node at that resolution if it were an order of magnitude rarer here. LIMITS: the wrapper adds a shell layer to every spawn, which may itself change timing; one scratch repo of 25 files; load is on this Mac, not the CI runner. POSITIVE CONTROLS (3 runs each, idle, same harness): pre-guard bundle (ef3fbe1) with ONE forced empty grep -n read: output silently diverged from the baseline in 3 of 3 code-map runs (the harness sees the fault); same for grep -l (3 of 3); the guarded bundle with the same single forced empty: 6 of 6 identical, the read executed twice (grep -n reads 15 vs 12 without the guard); guarded bundle with EVERY grep -n read empty: exit 7 in 3 of 3 code-map runs (callers unaffected, identical); forcing ls-files empty on the pre-guard bundle gave a non-zero exit in 3 of 6 command runs, i.e. an error, not a silent result. GENUINE EMPTY still answers: code-map with a task naming no repository token (grep -l exits 1) exits 0 with a result. RULE (opum-doc clarification to DEC-299 a5): ZERO empties observed under node, so (a5) stays at src/codemap.ts and the src/git.ts audit (gitRun, ls-files, cat-file --batch) is filed as a post-tag follow-up, subject to the leader/opum-doc reading of the detectable-rate limit above.
